label: Bark
text: Young trunks stay smooth for years. Old ones turn dark grayish brown, cut into broad ridges by deep furrows.

label: Needles
text: Three to six inches long, thin and soft, crowded toward the ends of the branches. Each stays two or three years, then drops in fall.

label: Pollen cones
text: Pollen cones grow in clusters at the branch tips in late spring. The young seed cones, yellow and in pairs, sit close by.

label: Cones
text: Slender brown cones, five to eight inches long, the scale tips beaded with white resin. Each takes two years to ripen.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray-brown to bronze on young trees, dotted with horizontal lenticels. It then splits into long, narrow plates whose edges curl away from the trunk.

label: Leaves
text: Feathery, 5 to 8 inches long, divided once into 15 to 30 small oval leaflets, or twice, into four to seven pairs of side branches of leaflets. The leaflets are shiny dark green above and yellow-green beneath.

label: Thorns
text: Wild trees grow stiff, branched thorns on the trunk and lower limbs. As a tree ages it stops making them in the upper and outer crown, but they keep coming on the lower trunk and its sprouts. The trees planted on campus are thornless selections.
source: Silvics of North America (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Pods
text: Flat, reddish-brown pods 12 to 18 inches long that twist into corkscrews and darken almost to black as they ripen. They hang on through the winter and are messy once they fall.

label: Flowers
text: Small, greenish-yellow flowers in narrow, hanging clusters two to three inches long, among the leaves in early summer. Easy to miss, but sweetly fragrant, and they last about two weeks.

label: Bark
text: Old trunks turn blocky or deeply furrowed toward the base. Where the bark is cut, the inner bark shows pinkish.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Leaves
text: Seven to eleven lobes, each ending in a bristle. They open pinkish red in spring, turn a glossy dark green, and finish russet to bright red.

label: Catkins
text: Male flowers hang in catkins as the leaves open. The female flowers are tiny spikes where the new leaves meet the twig.

label: Acorns
text: Barrel-shaped, three-quarters of an inch to an inch long, in a shallow cup that covers a quarter of the nut or less.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Young bark curls back in small papery strips. On old trunks it changes completely: dark reddish brown to nearly black, in thick, irregular scales.
source: Silvics of North America; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Two to three inches long, roughly triangular with a wedge-shaped base and doubly toothed edges, paler beneath. In a hard drought even old trees yellow and drop leaves early.

label: Catkins
text: The male catkins form at the twig tips in fall and wait through winter, opening in April or May. The female catkins come out with the leaves.

label: Seed catkins
text: Small upright cones packed with winged seeds. Once ripe and dry they shatter, scattering the seed.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Greenish gray and smooth on young trees, darkening and splitting lengthwise into tight, regular ridges with age.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Leaves
text: Three to six inches long, with five pointed lobes, a little broader than a sugar maple's, and dark green all summer.

label: Flowers
text: Rounded, upright clusters of small lime-yellow flowers open in April, before the leaves, in such numbers that it is one of the showiest trees of spring.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Fruit
text: Paired samaras ripening in October, each wing one to two inches long, the two spread almost in a straight line.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Older trunks turn dark gray-brown with blocky ridges. On young trees the peeling flakes show an orange inner bark.

label: Leaves
text: Three to seven inches long and widest beyond the middle, with shallow rounded lobes or coarse wavy teeth rather than deep lobes.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Catkins
text: Male flowers hang in clusters of catkins; the female flowers are tiny spikes where the leaves meet the twig.

label: Acorns
text: About an inch long, half enclosed in a warty cup. When the ripe acorn drops, the cup often stays behind on its stalk.

label: Bark
text: Rough from early on, soon breaking into irregular plates, and deeply fissured on the lower trunk.

label: Needles
text: Half an inch to an inch and a quarter long, rigid and four-sided, with lines of pores on every face. They stand out all round the shoot and sweep forward along its top.

label: Pollen cones
text: On most trees the pollen cones come out rose red, on a few yellowish green, and shed their pollen in May or June.

label: Cones
text: Two to four inches long, crowded in the upper crown. Young cones stand upright, turn to hang within a month, ripen by August, and shed seed from September into winter.
source: Silvics of North America; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown to dark gray, fissuring with age, on some trees deeply.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Three to six inches across and broadly five-sided in outline, in pairs on long stalks, dark green all summer.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Flowers
text: Small yellow flowers without petals hang on long, slender stalks, a week or two before the leaves; a tree in full bloom turns pale yellow all over. Trees seldom flower before about 22 years old.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Fruit
text: Paired samaras about an inch and a quarter long, the wings at a narrow angle, green until they ripen brown in October.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Smooth gray on young trees and branches. Old trunks turn dark gray and split lengthwise into scaly plates.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: About four inches long and as wide, with three to five lobes and irregular teeth. They unfold tinged red before deepening to dark green.

label: Flowers
text: One of the first trees to bloom, weeks before its own leaves. Some trees are all male, some all female, some both; the female flowers are the redder.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Fruit
text: Paired samaras an inch or two long that ripen in spring, not fall. Red maple sets a crop almost every year.
source: Morton Arboretum; Silvics of North America

label: Bark
text: Grayish to reddish brown, in stringy fibers that form a network of ridges and shallow furrows.
source: Morton Arboretum; Silvics of North America

label: Foliage
text: Tiny overlapping scales, about a twelfth of an inch, in soft, flat sprays at the ends of short, upturned branches.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Cones
text: About a third of an inch long, yellow ripening to light brown by September; open, they look like tiny roses. Only the middle two or three pairs of scales bear seed.
source: Morton Arboretum; Silvics of North America; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Winter color
text: Its foliage tends to discolor in winter, dulling from summer green; several garden forms were chosen for keeping their green.

label: Shape
text: Seventy to ninety feet tall but only ten to fifteen wide: dense and strictly columnar. Canker in the upper trunk often kills it before it is full grown.

label: Bark
text: Deeply furrowed, the trunk often swelling with large burls.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four and a half inches long, diamond-shaped to triangular, green on both sides, on stalks up to two inches. The thin, clear edge has shallow, rounded teeth, each tipped with a gland.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Catkins
text: Reddish male catkins two to three inches long with deep red anthers, hanging in early spring.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Bark
text: Dark and plated, furrowed between the plates, dark brown to nearly black.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Needles
text: Three to six inches long, two to a bundle, stiff and dark green, in heavy masses along the shoots.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Pollen cones
text: Pollen cones cluster on the new shoots in spring; they are not showy.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Cones
text: Two to three inches long, egg-shaped and stalkless, alone or in twos and threes, glossy brown when they ripen in their second year. The scales are ridged across, some ending in a short prickle.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray on young trees, developing shallow, dark fissures with age. Cut it and the inner bark is pinkish.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Glossy bright green above, paler below, with conspicuous tufts of brown hair where the veins meet. Every lobe ends in bristles.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Catkins
text: Male catkins grow from buds set the year before and open as the leaves develop; the female flowers sit on short stalks where this year's leaves meet the twig.

label: Acorns
text: Small, about half an inch, nearly round and often faintly striped, in a thin saucer of a cup that covers only a quarter of the nut.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown and fairly smooth at first; from about thirty years old it forms irregular, lumpy ridges. Shoots sometimes sprout from the trunk.

label: Leaves
text: An inch and a half to under three inches across, nearly round with a lopsided, heart-shaped base. Turn one over: pale bluish green beneath, with patches of rusty hair where the main veins meet.

label: Flowers
text: Five to eight flowers, sometimes many more, on a stalk joined to a narrow leafy bract. The clusters stand up above the leaves, which only one other linden's do.

label: Fruit
text: Small round nutlets about a quarter inch long, densely covered in brown hairs, with a thin, unribbed shell that breaks easily.

label: Bark
text: Reddish brown and soon rough on young trees, growing paler with age until the lower trunk is gray-brown in small, irregular plates.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Needles
text: Half an inch to an inch long, four-sided and sharp-tipped, glossy dark green.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Pollen cones
text: Small pinkish-red pollen cones cluster along the shoots. The young seed cones stand upright at the branch tips, reddish pink, then turn green and hang down once pollinated.

label: Cones
text: Cylindrical, purplish green while growing and light brown when ripe, hanging from the branch ends like ornaments.

label: Bark
text: Pale gray and dotted with lenticels when young. It soon scales finely to show yellow to reddish patches, and old trunks shed it in large, shaggy plates.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Leaves
text: Simple and alternate along the twig, each edge lined with sharp, regular teeth.

label: Flowers
text: Small and easily missed, opening in spring.

label: Fruit
text: A tiny, hard drupe about an eighth of an inch across, its surface netted with low ridges: no wing, as an elm's seed has.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Light gray with shallow ridges and furrows on younger trunks. The trunk often branches low into several upright limbs.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Up to three inches wide, on stalks an inch and a half to three and a half inches long. On short, stout spur shoots they come in clusters of three to five; on long shoots, one at a time.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Pollen cones
text: Only male trees bear them: short-stalked, catkin-like clusters about an inch long, on the spur shoots.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Seeds
text: Not a true fruit but a seed in a fleshy coat, yellowish green and plum-like, an inch to an inch and a half long. Cooked, the kernels are sold as street food in Korea.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Brownish gray, staying fairly smooth until about forty years of age, when it begins to fissure.

label: Leaves
text: On most northern trees the underside looks green, with only sparse hairs; farther south many trees have gray-green or whitish felt beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Hanging clusters of up to forty yellow-white flowers open in June and last about two weeks. One study counted 66 kinds of insects pollinating linden flowers.
source: Silvics of North America; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Fruit
text: Round to egg-shaped nutlets, a fifth to two-fifths of an inch across, hanging from a leafy bract three to six inches long. Wildlife eat the seeds.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Silvics of North America

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray when young. With age it splits into long, wide strips whose ends curl outward.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Three to six inches long, deeply cut into five lobes, on long stalks that let them twist in the wind.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Flowers
text: Dense clusters of petalless flowers, greenish yellow to pinkish red, open long before the leaves. Male and female flowers come in separate clusters, on the same tree or on different ones.
source: Silvics of North America; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Fruit
text: The largest seeds of any native maple: paired samaras about two inches long, the wings spread wide.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Slate gray and smooth, with a few fissures in old age, on a short trunk that is often crooked.
source: Silvics of North America; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Two and a half to five inches long, pointed, doubly toothed. They open reddish purple, turn dark green, and finish yellow to orange-red.

label: Catkins
text: Male catkins about an inch and a half long hang from short side shoots in April, green to brown with red on the scales; the small female catkins sit near the twig tips.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Fruit
text: Light brown nutlets, each under a three-lobed leafy bract like a small umbrella, in dangling clusters that ripen in October. The bract is lopsided, its inner lobe tiny.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Dark gray, cut into deep furrows between rough, rope-like ridges that cross and join.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Six to twelve inches long, made of eleven to nineteen oval leaflets, each with smooth edges and a tiny point at the tip. Bluish green, with little fall color.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Flowers
text: Pea flowers about three-quarters of an inch long, in hanging clusters that open after the leaves, in May or June. Bees do most of the pollinating.
source: Silvics of North America; Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Spines
text: On young stems a pair of stout spines, up to an inch long, flanks each bud.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Fibrous, reddish to gray-brown, in shallow vertical or interlacing ridges above a base fluted into sharp ridges.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum; Silvics of North America

label: Knees
text: Hollow, cone-shaped knees rise from the roots, crowded where soil meets deep water; their height tends to mark the usual flood level. Tests have mostly failed to show they bring air to the roots; they may instead brace the tree against floods.

label: Foliage
text: Soft, flat needles in two neat rows along slender side shoots. In late autumn the whole shoot drops, needles and all.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Cones
text: Small, round cones that grow and ripen in a single season and hang on the branches into winter.
source: Morton Arboretum; Silvics of North America

label: Buds
text: Big winter buds, a quarter to three-quarters of an inch long, varnished with sticky resin.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Five to seven leaflets, usually seven, spread like fingers from one stalk; each is four to ten inches long, widest near the tip and doubly toothed. They hold late and turn yellow.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Flowers
text: Upright clusters up to a foot high. Each white flower has a blotch at its base that starts yellow and turns red, with stamens longer than the petals.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Fruit
text: A spiny husk about two inches across, green ripening light brown in early fall, splitting to free one nut, sometimes two.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Look where branches meet the trunk for black, V-shaped marks. Twigs and young branches are dark reddish brown; the trunk turns fully white only once it has some girth.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches long, oval and pointed, with doubly toothed edges; dark green until they turn yellow in fall.

label: Catkins
text: Male catkins form in late summer, often in threes, and wait through winter before opening between mid-April and early June.
source: Silvics of North America; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Seed catkins
text: Slender hanging cylinders that fall apart when ripe. Birds pick at them so busily that some seed drops as early as July.

label: Bark
text: Flakes in fine scales of brown, gray and white, leaving a mottled trunk; the lower trunk of old trees turns rugged.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Leaves
text: Four to nine inches wide and leathery, with three to five shallow, maple-like lobes and broad teeth; bright green above, paler beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Dense round heads on long stalks, opening with the leaves: the male heads green, the female a bright burgundy red.
source: Morton Arboretum; Silvics of North America

label: Seed balls
text: Usually one to a stalk, about an inch across, packed with narrow seeds. Ripe by October, the ball holds on through winter, then breaks up in spring, each seed drifting off on its hairs.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Grayish black on mature trees and deeply furrowed.

label: Leaves
text: Two to five inches long with three to six pairs of rounded lobes and almost no stalk; at the base, two small ear-like lobes. Dark green above, grayish beneath.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Catkins
text: Male flowers hang in clusters of catkins; the female flowers are tiny spikes where leaves meet the twig.

label: Acorns
text: About an inch long, in a warty cup, one to several on a slender stalk two to five inches long. Trees may not bear until 20 or 30 years old.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Dark gray to brown, deeply furrowed between firm ridges. Even young twigs can grow corky ridges.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Four to ten inches long and widest near the tip, where one big wavy lobe can make up half the leaf; the lobes below are cut nearly to the midrib. Glossy dark green above, silvery green beneath.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Catkins
text: Male catkins hang from this year's shoots shortly after the leaves appear; the female flowers are small spikes where leaves meet the twig. Pollen from another tree takes better than its own.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Acorns
text: Three-quarters of an inch to an inch and a half long, half buried in the cup. They ripen in a single year and often sprout soon after they fall, and a bur oak goes on bearing them to 400 years of age.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Silvics of North America

label: Bark
text: Smooth, glossy and reddish brown, striped with long horizontal lenticels: a trunk easily taken for a cherry's.
source: Morton Arboretum; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Leaves
text: Two to six inches long, broadly oval, in pairs; dark green above, grayish green and net-veined beneath. They drop in fall with little change of color.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum

label: Flowers
text: Tiny creamy-white flowers, fragrant, packed into clusters six to twelve inches high.

label: Seed capsules
text: Dry, warty capsules about three-quarters of an inch long, green turning yellow, then brown, in enough numbers to notice in late summer.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark and thorns
text: Rough bark that grows slightly shaggy with age, on slender branches armed with thin, sharp thorns.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: One to three inches long, triangular with a heart-shaped base, lobed toward the base and sharply toothed. They unfold reddish purple before turning glossy dark green.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Flowers
text: Half-inch white flowers with pink anthers, in broad, flat clusters. It is the last of the common hawthorns to bloom, and the scent is unpleasant.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Fruit
text: Glossy scarlet haws about a quarter inch across, each holding three to five small stones.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Bark
text: Polished reddish to chestnut brown, banded with prominent horizontal lenticels.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; NC State Extension

label: Leaves
text: Three to five inches long, oval and drawn out to a long, slender point, sharply toothed, with a pair of glands on the stalk. They unfold purplish or bronze.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Flowers
text: Single flowers an inch and a quarter to an inch and a half across, deep blush pink, two to six together on stalks an inch long; each petal is notched at the tip.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Fruit
text: Egg-shaped, purple-black, under half an inch long.

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown, breaking into scaly ridges as the tree ages.

label: Leaves
text: In whorls of three, unequal even within one whorl, six inches to more than a foot long on stalks of four to six inches. Crushed, they have no smell.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Flowers
text: White bells striped orange and spotted purple inside, in upright clusters four to eight inches tall. It blooms earlier than the southern catalpa.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Pods
text: Eight to twenty inches long and packed with papery winged seeds, released when the pods split.

label: Bark
text: Reddish brown and rich in tannin: whole stands were once cut for the bark alone, to tan leather, until synthetic tannins replaced it in the 1940s.
source: Morton Arboretum; Silvics of North America

label: Needles
text: A quarter to two-thirds of an inch long on tiny stalks, finely toothed, mostly in two flat rows. A row of smaller needles lies along the top of the twig, often upside down, showing their white lines.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Pollen cones
text: Small, light-yellow, short-stalked clusters among the two-year-old needles, opening from late April to early June.

label: Cones
text: Half an inch to seven-eighths long, on short stalks, hanging from the branches like small ornaments.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Old trunks are thick and deeply fissured, reddish brown to dark gray-brown.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Needles
text: An inch to an inch and a half long, flat and short-stalked, with two whitish bands beneath. Crushed, they smell of camphor.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Pollen cones
text: Yellow pollen cones about three-quarters of an inch long, with reddish-brown scales at the base, clustered near the base of the new shoot; the seed cones form singly near its tip.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Silvics of North America

label: Cones
text: Hanging cones an inch and a half to four inches long, green ripening brown in a single season.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: The thin, flaky orange bark belongs to the crown. Lower down the trunk turns dark and blocky, cracked into plates or cut by joining furrows.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Needles
text: One to three inches long and stiff, with fine pale lines along the outer face, the pair joined at the base by a papery sheath about a quarter inch long.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum

label: Pollen cones
text: Clusters of yellow pollen cones shed their pollen from late May to early June.

label: Cones
text: One to three inches long on a short stalk, often lopsided at the base. The winged seeds are shed in spring.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Shallowly furrowed on young trees and more deeply on older ones, though few now live long enough to show it.

label: Leaves
text: Six to nine inches long, narrow, tapering about equally at both ends, dull green; yellow to yellow-brown in fall.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Catkins
text: Pencil-thin spikes six to eight inches long, crowded with small white male flowers, in July; the female flowers sit near their base. The smell is musty.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Burs
text: A bur of many slender, branched spines around one to three nuts, smaller than European chestnuts but said to taste better.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Medium to dark gray-brown, in deep, narrow ridges that interlace.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Leaves
text: One to two feet long, made of many leaflets; the one at the tip is often missing. Yellow in fall.

label: Catkins
text: Slender male catkins hang from last year's shoots; the female flowers sit in short spikes at the tips of the new ones. On most trees the female flowers open first, which makes self-pollination unlikely.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Nuts
text: A round, yellow-green husk up to two inches across around a single nut. It ripens in September or October and drops soon after the leaves.
source: Morton Arboretum; Silvics of North America

label: Bark
text: Brown, with orange-red beneath; older bark sheds to show the red inner layer.

label: Leaves
text: Three to five inches long and often wider than long, heart-shaped with a short point and smooth edges; clear yellow in fall.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Flowers
text: Small pea-shaped flowers, rose pink to reddish purple, rarely white. Two or three weeks after they open the leaves come out and the flowers fall.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Pods
text: Flat pea pods two to three inches long, full-grown by midsummer.
source: Morton Arboretum; Silvics of North America

label: Bark
text: Narrow, flat ridges and plates that spread outward at their lower ends, giving the trunk a shaggy look. Large patches are often smooth, the work of a harmless fungus called smooth patch.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Leaves
text: Five to nine inches long with five to nine rounded lobes, some shallow, some deep. They unfold pinkish, turn dark green, and finish wine red.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Catkins
text: Yellowish male catkins two to three inches long appear as the leaves open; the small reddish female flowers follow five to ten days later, singly or in pairs.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Acorns
text: About three-quarters of an inch to an inch long, stalkless, alone or in pairs, in a shallow cup of warty scales.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray with pale, shallow fissures on young trees; fissured from about 25 years, and craggy, browner and scaly in old age.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Three to eight inches long, glossy above and pale beneath, usually four-lobed with the tip cut straight across. Golden yellow in fall.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Flowers
text: Cups about two inches tall, yellow-green with an orange band near the base of each petal. Flies, beetles and bees pollinate them.
source: Morton Arboretum; Silvics of North America

label: Fruit
text: An upright, cone-like cluster about three inches long, made of narrow winged seeds.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Pale silvery gray and smooth. Unusually for a beech, it can sucker from the roots, forming dense thickets of one clone.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Leaves
text: Two to five inches long, with nine to fourteen pairs of straight side veins, each ending in a small tooth. Golden bronze in fall.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Buds
text: Slender, sharply pointed and over an inch long, wrapped in light brown scales.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Flowers and nuts
text: Male flowers dangle in long-stalked round heads as the leaves unfold; the females sit in twos to fours. By fall a prickly bur holds two or three triangular nuts, and opens after the first hard frosts.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Smooth and pale gray on young trees; from about thirty years it develops flat-topped ridges that cross one another.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches long, nearly round with a heart-shaped base and sharp teeth. The white underside is a felt of tiny star-shaped hairs; the young twigs are felted gray too.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Flowers
text: Creamy yellow, strongly honey-scented, four to ten to a drooping cluster, each cluster hung from a long strap-shaped bract felted white on one side.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Fruit
text: Egg-shaped nutlets about a third of an inch long, densely felted gray-brown, with a thick, woody shell.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Orange-brown on young trees, peeling in long fibrous strips; grayer on old ones. The base of the trunk flares into buttresses and flutes.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Needles
text: Soft, flat needles about half an inch long, set in opposite pairs on side shoots that drop whole in fall, after turning bronze, orange or rust red.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Pollen cones
text: Tiny egg-shaped pollen cones, under a quarter inch long, shed their pollen in late winter before the leaves.

label: Cones
text: Nearly round, half an inch to an inch across, with eight to twelve pairs of opposite scales, hanging on long stalks. Purplish black when young, brown when ripe in October.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark and twigs
text: Grayish brown, soon cracked into rugged vertical ridges. From their second year the twigs often grow corky wings.

label: Leaves
text: The pointed lobes have finely toothed edges, and small tufts of hair often sit where the veins meet beneath. Fall color starts late, and in mild places the leaves can hang on until March.

label: Flowers
text: Small greenish flowers in heads, March to May: the male heads in a short upright spike, the female in a single larger ball on a drooping stalk.
source: Silvics of North America; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Gum balls
text: A woody ball an inch or more across, glossy green fading to yellow, made of many beaked capsules. They open in fall to free small winged seeds, and the empty balls hang on all winter.
source: Silvics of North America; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Gray to brown, soon broken into narrow, very scaly strips that shred lengthwise.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Leaves
text: Two to five inches long, oval, sharply and often doubly toothed, with twelve to fifteen pairs of side veins. Like a hornbeam's, but the bark tells them apart.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Catkins
text: One to three male catkins form at the branch tips in late summer and hang through winter, shedding pollen in spring; the small female catkins appear with the leaves.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Fruit
text: Drooping clusters one to three inches long of inflated, papery sacs, each holding a hard nutlet, creamy green turning tan. They break up from late summer, scattering seed into winter.
source: Morton Arboretum; Silvics of North America; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Pale gray-brown with close, mostly vertical, scaly ridges; young twigs are purplish with a waxy bloom.

label: Leaves
text: One to three inches long, rounded to egg-shaped with a blunt tip, smooth-edged, with six to eleven pairs of parallel side veins.

label: Smoke
text: The flowers are tiny and yellowish; the smoke is what follows. The branched flower stalks lengthen into plumes six to eight inches tall, covered in long silky hairs, pinkish or yellowish fading to pale gray.

label: Fruit
text: Small dry fruits, about a fifth of an inch across and prominently veined, scattered through the smoky plumes.

label: Bark
text: Gray to pale brown, with shallow lengthwise fissures; the branchlets often grow corky ridges.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches long, in pairs, with three to five broad lobes, rounded or pointed at the tip, the edges smooth or wavy rather than toothed. Pale green beneath.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Flowers
text: Small yellow-green flowers in upright clusters, opening in April after the leaves; they are easy to overlook.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Fruit
text: Paired samaras about an inch long, the wings spread out in a straight line, ripening in October.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Thin, smooth and shining on young trees; on old trunks, shallow irregular fissures with flat, light brown scales. The inner bark is pinkish.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Leaves
text: Three to eight inches long, oblong and unlobed, widest near the middle, ending in a single bristle. Dead leaves often hang on through the whole winter.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Catkins
text: Male flowers dangle in catkins; the smaller female flowers are held close against the twig.

label: Acorns
text: Half to two-thirds of an inch long, nearly round and often striped, a third to half covered by a thin cup.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Gray and smooth at first, becoming slightly ridged; stout, stiff twigs, purple-brown on some plants.

label: Leaves
text: Three to eight inches long, in pairs, oval to oblong with smooth edges; glossy dark green above, paler beneath, with hairs at least on the veins.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Flowers
text: Each white flower splits into four narrow straps half an inch to an inch and a half long, slightly fragrant, in soft clusters in late spring.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Fruit
text: Egg-shaped drupes about half an inch long, dark blue with a powdery bloom, ripening in late summer on female trees.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Bark
text: Yellowish brown and metallic, peeling in thin curls and marked with long horizontal lenticels. On old trees it turns black, still peeling.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Leaves
text: Three to five inches long, oval with a long point, doubly toothed. The inner bark of the twigs tastes of wintergreen.
source: Morton Arboretum; Silvics of North America

label: Catkins
text: Male catkins form in late summer in twos or threes at the twig tips and open in spring, two to four inches long, shedding pollen for only three to five days. The small green female catkins come out with the leaves.
source: Silvics of North America; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Seed catkins
text: Upright, egg-shaped catkins about an inch long, woody and hairy-scaled, packed with tiny winged seeds; they shatter over the winter.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Brown to gray when young; side branches often end in a thorn.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: An inch and a half to three inches long, oval and pointed, finely toothed, mostly in pairs or nearly so. They stay green well into autumn, after most trees are bare.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Flowers
text: Small light-green flowers with four sepals in a cross, in dense clusters at the base of the young shoots.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Fruit
text: Black, about a quarter inch across, crowded along the branches. Animals eat them and spread the seed.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Brown and shiny on young trees, gray-brown and lightly furrowed at maturity. Wild thickets are often thorny.
source: Morton Arboretum; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Leaves
text: An inch and a half to three inches long, broadly oval with a pointed tip, leathery and glossy dark green.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Flowers
text: White, five-petaled, five-eighths to three-quarters of an inch across, six to twelve to a cluster, with a disagreeable smell. In bloom it is often mistaken for serviceberry or crabapple.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Fruit
text: Small, hard, russet-dotted pears under half an inch, in heavy crops. Birds eat them and carry the seed into fields and woods.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Gray and smooth with raised lenticels on younger wood, turning brown and scaly on older trunks.

label: Leaves
text: Oval with a rounded base, two to five inches long, irregularly saw-toothed and usually hairy beneath.
source: Canadian Food Inspection Agency, The Biology of Malus domestica

label: Flowers
text: Four to six in a cluster, mostly at the tips of short spur shoots: five petals, white to deep pink, about twenty stamens with yellow anthers. Bees do most of the pollinating.
source: Canadian Food Inspection Agency, The Biology of Malus domestica

label: Fruit
text: A pome, usually over two inches across, dimpled at the stalk and usually at the other end too.
source: Canadian Food Inspection Agency, The Biology of Malus domestica

label: Stems
text: A shrub or small tree with a short, thick trunk and crooked, wide-spreading branches.

label: Leaves
text: Three to six inches long, broad and uneven at the base, with wavy or toothed edges. They turn yellow and often hang on while the flowers open, hiding them.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Flowers
text: Two to four together on a short stalk, each with four crumpled, strap-shaped yellow petals half an inch to two-thirds of an inch long, from September into November. They are fragrant.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Seed capsules
text: Woody, hairy capsules about half an inch long, dull orange-brown with four sharp, curved points, ripening a year after the flower, as the next year's flowers open.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Dark brown and rough, breaking into scaly plates whose edges curl outward.
source: Morton Arboretum; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Leaves
text: Huge and twice-divided, up to three feet long and two wide, with many oval blue-green leaflets; the lowest division is a single leaflet. Mild yellow in fall.
source: Morton Arboretum; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Flowers
text: Greenish-white flowers in branched clusters as the leaves come out, male and female usually on separate trees. The male clusters are three to four inches long, with bright orange anthers.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum

label: Pods
text: Leathery, reddish-brown pods five to ten inches long holding a few large, round seeds, on female trees only.

label: Bark
text: Light gray, loosely ridged and furrowed.

label: Leaves
text: Opposite and compound, with five to nine leaflets; yellow or yellow-green in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Small flowers in clusters with or just before the leaves, male and female on separate trees. A male tree sheds its pollen over only three or four days.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Fruit
text: Long, narrow, single-seeded samaras in clusters on female trees, full-sized within a month of flowering.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Pale gray and smooth on a short trunk, with branches that sweep low.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches long, oval, with five to eight pairs of veins and an edge fringed with fine hairs, barely toothed. Glossy dark green, russet to bronze in fall.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Flowers
text: Small and easily missed: male flowers hang in clusters, females sit in pairs in a bristly cup, both on the same tree.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Nuts
text: A prickly husk with soft, needle-like scales, usually holding two three-sided, edible nuts.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Grayish brown, peeling in large, irregular scales with age to leave a patchwork of yellows and browns.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches long, in pairs, oval with smooth edges; reddish purple in fall.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Flowers
text: What look like four white petals are pointed bracts an inch or two long, held above the leaves in June and lasting several weeks; the true flowers are a small knot in the middle.

label: Fruit
text: A raspberry-like ball about an inch across, ripening in August.

label: Bark
text: Light gray, flaky, turning slightly shaggy on older trunks.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches long, round and heart-shaped with small rounded teeth, set in neat pairs along arching branches. They unfold reddish purple before turning blue-green.
source: Morton Arboretum; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Flowers
text: Male and female flowers on separate trees, small and red: the male open in spring before the leaves, the female a little later, as the leaves expand.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum

label: Pods
text: Small, narrow pods about three-quarters of an inch to an inch long, on female trees only.
source: Morton Arboretum; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Stems
text: Several brown stems from the base; the shrub is slow to leaf out in spring.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches long, sharply toothed except near the base, glossy dark green above and paler beneath; golden yellow in fall.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum

label: Flowers
text: Five-petaled flowers in upright spikes two to six inches long at the branch tips, white or pink, lasting four to six weeks in midsummer. Butterflies come for the nectar.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum

label: Seed capsules
text: Tiny dry capsules, about an eighth of an inch, in slender spikes that last through winter. Goldfinches, robins and warblers pick at them.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Green on young stems, turning gray-brown and splitting into shallow ridges with age.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Leaves
text: Opposite, six to eight inches long, made of three to five (sometimes seven) irregularly toothed leaflets; light green, with little fall color.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Flowers
text: Male and female flowers on separate trees, with or before the leaves: the male in tight bundles, the female in drooping strings.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Fruit
text: Paired samaras in hanging clusters, on female trees only. They ripen from August to October and keep falling until spring.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Stems
text: Usually a crowd of upright stems, sometimes one trunk, the bark peeling in spiraling flakes. It spreads freely by root suckers.

label: Leaves
text: Two to five inches long, in pairs, pointed and heart-shaped to oval, smooth-edged, dark gray-green to blue-green; yellow in fall.
source: Morton Arboretum; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Flowers
text: Tubular, four-lobed flowers in conical clusters six to eight inches long, usually in pairs at the shoot tips; lilac, purple or white in the wild type, and in many more shades and doubles in its cultivars.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Seed capsules
text: Flattened, smooth, pointed brown capsules up to three-quarters of an inch long, in clusters that split and hang on into winter.
source: Morton Arboretum; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Bark
text: Flakes away in patches, smooth beneath, in a mix of gray, orange and reddish brown.

label: Leaves
text: Two to three and a half inches long, oval and pointed, with small, widely spaced teeth; fall color ranges from yellow to red to reddish purple.

label: Flowers
text: White, cup-shaped to flat, about two and a half inches across, with orange anthers, in early to midsummer. Pseudocamellia means false camellia: the two are in the same family.

label: Seed capsules
text: Brown, egg-shaped capsules about an inch long that split to release seed and stay on the tree.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray, streaked white by lenticels; older bark turns slightly rough.

label: Leaves
text: Five to nine inches long, with nine to fifteen narrow, toothed leaflets, smooth-edged near their base. The winter buds are woolly.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum

label: Flowers
text: Small five-petaled white flowers in flat-topped clusters in May, with a slightly unpleasant smell. Butterflies visit them.

label: Fruit
text: Berry-like fruits a quarter to a third of an inch across, yellow to red, in showy clusters; a favorite of many birds.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Dark gray to almost black; on old trunks the scaly plates flip up at the edges. Young bark tastes bitter and aromatic.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Two to five and a half inches long, narrow and tapering at both ends, finely toothed, with small glands near the base. Yellow and orange in fall.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Flowers
text: Small white flowers in hanging spikes four to six inches long, opening in late May when the leaves are nearly full-grown, unlike garden cherries that bloom on bare twigs. The smell is slightly unpleasant.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Fruit
text: Dark, pea-sized cherries along the spikes in late summer.

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown, deeply ridged and furrowed in a corky pattern that grows stronger with age.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: In pairs, ten to fifteen inches long, with five to eleven smooth-edged, long-pointed leaflets, glossy dark green and clear yellow in fall. The leafstalk's base nearly hides the bud.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum

label: Flowers
text: Small yellow-green flowers about a quarter inch across, in wide clusters in late spring, male and female on separate trees.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Fruit
text: Round fruits about half an inch across, yellowish turning black, with a strong smell when crushed. Only female trees bear them, and birds spread the seed.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Red-brown with white stripes on young trees, in a rough diamond pattern; older trunks develop ridges and furrows.

label: Leaves
text: Two to six inches long, oval to oblong with fine teeth; dark green above, pale and a little downy beneath.
source: Virginia Tech Dendrology; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Flowers
text: White bells about an inch long, four-lobed, on slender stalks in clusters of two to six, hanging along last year's twigs in spring.
source: Virginia Tech Dendrology; Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Fruit
text: A dry, corky drupe an inch and a half to two inches long with four equal wings, ripening in autumn and hanging on to scatter over winter.
source: Virginia Tech Dendrology; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown and broken into small blocks; where a piece sheds it shows darker bark beneath.

label: Leaves
text: In pairs, rounded with a pointed tip and wavy edges. The veins curve toward the tip without reaching the edge, the mark of a dogwood.

label: Flowers
text: The four white bracts, sometimes pink, are not petals; the true flowers are the small cluster in the middle. Florida is Latin for flowering.
source: Morton Arboretum; Silvics of North America

label: Fruit
text: Clusters of bright red fruit, ripe from July through August: poisonous to people, but eaten by a great variety of wildlife.
source: Morton Arboretum; Silvics of North America

label: Bark
text: Thin, smooth and pale gray, patterned with small round lenticels.

label: Leaves
text: Eight to twelve inches long, with seven to eleven smooth-edged leaflets set alternately along the stalk, the end one largest. The swollen base of each leafstalk hides next year's bud all summer.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Flowers
text: White pea flowers with a pale yellow blotch, in hanging clusters, sweetly scented of vanilla.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Pods
text: Flat, light brown pods two and a half to four inches long, holding four to six seeds; they fall a little after the leaves.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Bark
text: Gray and rough, studded with warty, corky outgrowths.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four and a half inches long, egg-shaped and drawn out to a point, the base rounded or heart-shaped and often lopsided.

label: Flowers
text: Small greenish flowers, with or just after the leaves, in late May this far north.

label: Fruit
text: Round drupes about a third of an inch across: a thin pulp over a single bony stone. Ripe in September and October, many hang on until spring.
source: Silvics of North America; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Reddish brown and shedding, but thin, so it never furrows deeply.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Foliage
text: Scales an eighth to a quarter inch long, pressed close in four rows, sharp-pointed, with no white marks beneath. The sprays feel rough, and smell unpleasant when crushed.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Pollen cones
text: Tiny yellow or reddish pollen cones at the tips of the shoots, shedding pollen from mid-April to late May.

label: Cones
text: Round cones about half an inch across, usually of four scales, each with a pointed boss. Most take two years to ripen, so this year's and last year's hang side by side.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Smooth, shiny and reddish brown on young trees, with rows of pale lenticels; on old trunks nearly black and broken into scaly plates.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Two to six inches long, oval with a heart-shaped base on short shoots, twelve to eighteen pairs of veins, the teeth curving forward. Crushed, they smell of wintergreen.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum; Silvics of North America

label: Catkins
text: Male catkins form in late summer and wait through winter, opening in April or May two to three inches long at the twig tips. The female catkins come with the leaves, on short spur shoots.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Seed catkins
text: Upright catkins packed with tiny winged seeds that ripen from mid-August and fall from mid-September into November.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Orange-brown to cinnamon, peeling in curved, papery plates, and in round scales on older trunks.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Leaves
text: Three leaflets, three to five inches overall: the middle one short-stalked and coarsely toothed, the side ones nearly stalkless. Blue-green above, pale to whitish beneath, which gives it the name griseum, gray.

label: Flowers
text: Small yellow-green flowers, usually three to a hanging cluster, as the leaves expand.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Fruit
text: Samaras an inch to an inch and a quarter long, the wings at a narrow to right angle, hanging into winter. The seed inside is often empty.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Gray and fairly smooth on young trees; older trunks thicken into a distinctly corky bark.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Needles
text: Flat, attached singly, curving outward and up from the twig, with pores on the upper side as well as the lower. Crushed, they smell of lemon.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Pollen cones
text: Reddish pollen cones under half an inch long, crowded on the underside of last year's twigs around mid-crown, opening in May or June.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Cones
text: Upright, cylindrical cones three to five inches long, high in the crown, green or purplish turning brown when ripe in late summer.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Pale gray and smooth on young trees, with prominent resin blisters; old trunks turn dark gray-brown and flaky.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Needles
text: Flat, dark green, attached singly; on lower branches they spread in two rows, higher up they point forward. Crushed, they give off a strong balsam scent.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Pollen cones
text: Yellowish-red pollen cones tinged purple, in dense clusters along the undersides of last year's twigs, opening in late May or early June.
source: Silvics of North America; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Cones
text: Upright cones an inch to two and a half inches long, violet-purple ripening purplish brown. When ripe the scales fall away, leaving the bare central spike on the branch.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Gray and smooth for many years, becoming furrowed into coarse ridges on old trunks.

label: Leaves
text: Three to seven inches, slender-pointed and sometimes three-lobed toward the tip, coarsely double-toothed, with fourteen to twenty pairs of veins. The base is very lopsided, its rounded half often hiding the short stalk.

label: Flowers
text: Small reddish-green flowers in tight clusters on the bare twigs in early spring.

label: Fruit
text: Flat, papery, rounded samaras with the seed at the center, in crowded green clusters that ripen in late spring.

label: Bark
text: Reddish brown to gray-brown, deeply ridged and furrowed with age.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Three to seven inches long and smooth-edged; all three shapes can share a single branch. Fall color runs yellow, orange or scarlet. Dried and ground, the leaves are filé powder, used in Creole cooking.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Flowers
text: Greenish-yellow flowers in loose, drooping clusters in March and April as the leaves unfold, male and female on separate trees.
source: Silvics of North America; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Fruit
text: Dark blue drupes under half an inch long, each in a red cup on a thick red stalk, on female trees only.
source: Silvics of North America; Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Light gray to silvery gray, flaking in loose scales.

label: Leaves
text: Up to eight inches long, widest near the tip, with coarse, regular, rounded teeth; white and hairy beneath, red in fall.

label: Catkins
text: Male flowers in dangling catkins and smaller female flowers close to the twig, opening with the leaves in April and May.
source: Morton Arboretum; Silvics of North America

label: Acorns
text: An inch to an inch and a half long, nearly stalkless, a third covered by a broad cup of free, hairy scales. Sweet enough that cows eat them, hence cow oak; they fall in September and October.
source: Silvics of North America; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown, sometimes peeling, marked with prominent horizontal lenticels.

label: Leaves
text: Two to five inches, oval and finely toothed, smooth and green, sometimes with two small glands at the base of the blade.

label: Flowers
text: White, five-petaled flowers on long stalks, three to five together, in late spring.

label: Fruit
text: Round, bright red cherries with a single stone, hanging on long stalks.

label: Leaves
text: One to three and a half inches long, leathery and glossy, widest above the middle and tapering to both ends, with small round teeth. New growth comes bronze to red.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Flowers
text: Small white urns about a quarter inch long, hanging from slender drooping clusters three to six inches long in March and April; frost often damages them.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Seed capsules
text: Dry seed pods follow the flowers on most plants; a few sterile cultivars set none.

label: Stems
text: Smooth, hairless young stems; it is told from mountain pieris by these bare stems, its narrower leaves and its hanging flower clusters.

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown, soon deeply fissured into rugged but fairly regular blocks; the trunk does not flare at the base as the swamp tupelos' do.

label: Leaves
text: Three to six inches long, variable in shape, smooth-edged or with a few teeth, glossy above and dull beneath, on short stalks; often bright red in fall.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Flowers
text: Small greenish-white flowers, April to June, the male in clusters of two to five, the female in fewer; most trees are male or female.
source: Silvics of North America; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Fruit
text: Blue-black, waxy-bloomed drupes about half an inch long, alone or in twos and threes, ripening in September and October.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Silvics of North America

label: Bark
text: Fairly smooth with visible lenticels on young trees; on old trees gray, furrowed, the fissures showing orange inner bark.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Egg-shaped on one shoot, three- to five-lobed on the next, always toothed; dark green, with inconsistent yellow fall color.
source: Morton Arboretum; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Catkins
text: Small pale-green catkins in late spring, male and female usually on separate trees. The male flowers release their pollen explosively.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Fruit
text: Clustered fruits under an inch long, red at first and ripening dark purple, black or greenish white. Birds and squirrels spread them, which is how it escapes into the wild.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Bark
text: Young branches smooth and green; older bark dark gray and smooth.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Three to five inches long and oblong, smooth-edged, glossy dark green above with a silvery-gray bloom beneath.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum

label: Flowers
text: Creamy white cups two to three inches across, one at a time from mid-June over many weeks, lemon-scented and often half hidden among the leaves.
source: Morton Arboretum; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Fruit
text: A pickle-shaped cluster about two inches long, green turning pink then red, splitting to show bright red seeds.
source: Morton Arboretum; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Stems
text: Dark brown with a hint of green on mature stems. Twigs, like nearly every part, give off a strong, pleasant smell when crushed.
source: Morton Arboretum; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Leaves
text: Two to six inches long, widest above the middle, tapering to both ends, with slightly wavy edges; they stay green long into fall before turning yellow. Spicebush swallowtail caterpillars feed on them.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum

label: Flowers
text: Small clusters of pale yellow-green flowers on bare twigs before the leaves; butterflies visit them.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum

label: Fruit
text: Scarlet, oval, under half an inch, ripening from July to October; rich in fat, they are eaten quickly by birds.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum

label: Stems
text: Many stems in a vase shape; young twigs densely hairy, the older bark peeling in large thin sheets, most toward the base.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Leaves
text: One to three inches long, in pairs, broadly oval and nearly smooth-edged, dull blue-green, downy on both sides when young.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Flowers
text: Pink bells about half an inch long, flaring at the mouth, yellow-veined in the throat, usually in pairs on very hairy stalks; that hairiness tells it from weigela.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Fruit
text: Small, bristly brown capsules about a quarter inch long, each holding a single seed, in loose clusters.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown and smooth when young. The young shoots glisten with silvery scales, and the branches sometimes carry spines.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: One to three and a half inches long and narrow, like a willow's, pale green above and silvery beneath.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Flowers
text: Small sweet-smelling bells, one to three where leaves meet the stem, silvery outside and yellow inside, in mid to late spring.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Fruit
text: Oval, about half an inch long, yellow with silvery scales. Many kinds of birds eat them and spread the seed.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Bark
text: Pale gray, quickly breaking into small corky plates and finally deep vertical fissures.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Leaves
text: Two and a half to six inches long, egg-shaped with a pointed tip and heart-shaped base, toothed, hairy on the veins beneath; pale yellow in fall.

label: Catkins
text: Male catkins two to three inches long; the female flowers are small and easily missed.

label: Nuts
text: Thick-shelled nuts about half an inch across in close clusters, each in a spreading husk up to an inch and a half wide, cut into many narrow, jagged lobes and set with stiff glandular hairs.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Bark
text: Dark brown and somewhat scaly, flaking on older stems.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches long, in pairs, oval, with three to five pairs of curving veins. Fall color is usually poor, many leaves dropping green.

label: Flowers
text: Short-stalked clusters of tiny yellow flowers, each cluster first wrapped in four bracts, opening on bare twigs in very early spring and shrugging off freezing weather.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Fruit
text: Oblong drupes about two-thirds of an inch long, bright cherry red, ripening in midsummer.

label: Bark
text: Wine-purple to brown on young stems, with vertical tan lenticels; older trunks turn corky, in small rectangular plates.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: About four inches long, oval with wavy edges, whitish beneath. They alternate along the twig but crowd at its tip, so they look whorled. Burgundy red in fall.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum

label: Flowers
text: Small creamy-white flowers, fifty to a hundred together in flat-topped clusters two to six inches across, in May and June.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Fruit
text: Berries about a quarter inch across, green to white and finally blue-black, on stalks that turn red; ripe in July. Many birds come for them.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Smooth steel gray with fine vertical silver markings, the trunk and old branches fluted.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Leaves
text: Two to five inches long, sharply double-toothed, with ten to eighteen pairs of straight, deeply impressed veins; yellow late in fall.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum

label: Catkins
text: Yellowish male catkins about an inch long hang in April; the greenish female catkins near the twig tips stretch to two or three inches as they fruit.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Fruit
text: A small ribbed nutlet at the base of each three-lobed leafy bract, nearly symmetrical, in hanging clusters that ripen yellow-brown in October.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray on the main trunk; the thin young twigs are often bright red.
source: Morton Arboretum; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Leaves
text: Two to five inches long, in pairs, cut two-thirds or more of the way in into five to nine sharply double-toothed lobes. Green, red or purple, finely dissected in some forms; scarlet, orange or yellow in fall.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum

label: Flowers
text: Small red to purple flowers in loose, upright clusters as the new leaves open.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Fruit
text: Paired samaras half to three-quarters of an inch long.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Bark
text: Gray and smooth for many years, then scaly and split lengthwise, brownish or blackish gray on old trees.

label: Needles
text: Dense, about an inch long; on the lower side they spread in rows, on top they sweep forward and hide the shoot.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Pollen cones
text: Crowded, hanging pollen cones under an inch long, yellowish.

label: Cones
text: Upright cones four to six inches long, greenish yellow ripening reddish then brown, with the tips of the bracts poking out and bent back between the scales.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Bark
text: Smooth and brown-gray when young; on old stems gray-black and broken into small, flat-topped blocks.

label: Leaves
text: Three to four inches long, oval with a pointed tip and fine teeth, glossy, in opposite pairs, much like a plum's. Showy red to purple in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Flat clusters four to five inches across of small, strongly fragrant white flowers with long yellowish stamens, in May and June.

label: Fruit
text: Oval, a third of an inch long, green, yellow and pink in the same cluster before they turn blue-black in September and October. Each holds one flat stone.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches long, pointed and finely toothed, glossy dark green, the new growth yellow-green.

label: Flowers
text: Flat-topped clusters three to four inches across of quarter-inch creamy flowers, five-petaled, with long stamens.

label: Fruit
text: Half-inch fruits in pale green, yellow and pink, all in the same cluster, that slowly turn blue-black on red stalks.

label: Fall color
text: Orange to purplish red.

label: Stems
text: Young canes are often red; old stems have gray-brown, thinly furrowed bark.

label: Leaves
text: Oval and smooth-edged, reddish green in spring, blue-green in summer with paler undersides. Fall color is a fine mix of red, yellow, orange and purple.

label: Flowers
text: Small white or pink bells hanging in clusters in spring.

label: Berries
text: Round, blue to purple berries, each crowned with a little star where the flower was, ripening from green through pink in August.

label: Bark
text: Gray, in narrow flat ridges and shallow furrows, with reddish-brown inner bark showing in the cracks. The twigs are downy.

label: Leaves
text: Four to eight inches, broad, with a lopsided base, rough on top from tiny hairs. Turn one over: it is whitish and downy, with very prominent pale veins.

label: Flowers
text: Dense clusters of five to twenty greenish-red flowers on short stems, on the bare twigs in early spring.

label: Fruit
text: Flat, round, one-seeded samaras with the seed in the middle, ripening in spring.

label: Bark
text: Light gray-brown with irregular furrows, often streaked dark by weeping wetwood. Mature trunks are dark gray with shallow grooves.

label: Leaves
text: Small, one to three inches, oval to lance-shaped, only slightly lopsided at the base. Dark green above, light green beneath. Yellow in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Light green to reddish flowers in tight clusters of two to five, on the bare twigs in early spring, before the leaves.

label: Fruit
text: Round papery samaras half an inch to an inch across, one seed in the middle, crowded along the twigs and scattered by the wind.

label: Bark
text: Gray, in flat ridges that braid and interlace up the trunk. Firm on most trees, flaking on old ones.

label: Leaves
text: Four to six inches long, oval with a long, slightly curved point, rough to the touch, doubly toothed, and lopsided at the base. A plain yellow in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Small greenish-red flowers in drooping clusters of three or four, on the bare twigs early in spring.

label: Fruit
text: Wafer-like samaras, each tiny seed in a flat, oval, papery wing, in clusters on long stalks, ripe as the leaves reach full size.

label: Bark
text: Gray and smooth on young trees, becoming shallowly fissured with age.

label: Leaves
text: About five inches long, heart-shaped with a pointed tip, medium to dark green above, light green and softly hairy beneath. Pale yellow in fall.

label: Flowers
text: Drooping clusters three to four inches long of fragrant, pale yellow flowers with many stamens, hanging from a leafy bract in June.

label: Fruit
text: Small, gray, oval nutlets with raised ribs, ripening in late summer beneath the bract.

label: Bark
text: Red-brown and peeling in thin scales, on a trunk that grows short and enormously thick with age.

label: Needles
text: Flat, half an inch to an inch and a half long, set in two rows on either side of the shoot; shiny dark green above and yellowish green beneath, with no white bands.

label: Pollen cones
text: Male plants carry small pollen cones where the needles join the shoot, beneath it.

label: Seeds
text: On female plants, single seeds sit in a red, fleshy cup, the aril, open at the end. The seed inside, like the needles, is poisonous.

label: Bark
text: Grayish brown, cut by deep furrows between interlacing ridges; the furrows show reddish brown.

label: Leaves
text: Six to ten inches long, with 7 to 17 smooth-edged leaflets an inch or two long, pointed, green above and paler beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Small, creamy white pea flowers, lightly fragrant, in loose sprays six to twelve inches long at the branch tips in July and August.

label: Pods
text: Hanging pods three to eight inches long, bright green and smooth, then yellow-brown, holding one to six seeds. They hang on into winter.

label: Stems
text: Yellowish gray to light gray-brown, warty with short raised lenticels.

label: Leaves
text: In opposite pairs, compound, usually of seven sharply toothed leaflets two to six inches long, set in pairs with one at the tip.

label: Flowers
text: Many quarter-inch, fragrant, creamy-white flowers in flat to rounded clusters four to ten inches across, in June.

label: Fruit
text: Quarter-inch purple-black berries, each with three to five small stones, in large drooping clusters in August and September.

label: Bark
text: Light orange-brown to dark brown or nearly black, with deep grooves and, on old trees, rough, shaggy scales.

label: Leaves
text: Three to six inches long and only half to three-quarters of an inch wide, finely toothed, tapering to a long point. Medium to dark green on both sides.

label: Catkins
text: Male and female catkins up to two inches long, on separate trees, open as the leaves emerge, late March and April.

label: Seed capsules
text: Small reddish-brown capsules that split open to release hundreds of tiny seeds, each tufted with down that carries it on the wind.

label: Shape
text: Broad and rounded, the long slender branchlets hanging straight down, often to the ground, like a curtain.

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown to gray-black, rough with irregular furrows.

label: Leaves
text: Three to six inches long, very narrow, finely toothed and long-pointed, light green above and grayish green to whitish beneath.

label: Catkins
text: Slender, silvery-green to yellow catkins one to two inches long along the hanging shoots in April and May, males and females on separate trees.

label: Bark
text: Gray to yellowish brown, corky, and furrowed into ridges.

label: Leaves
text: An inch and a half to four inches long and narrow, finely toothed, tapering. Medium to dark green above; silky white hairs make the underside white.

label: Catkins
text: In April and May, on separate trees: male catkins up to two inches long with yellow anthers, and greenish female catkins up to an inch and a half.

label: Seed capsules
text: By midsummer the female catkins are strings of small two-part capsules, splitting to release tiny seeds with silky hairs.

label: Stems
text: Young branches are covered in reddish-brown hairs, like the velvet on a stag's antlers. Older stems turn gray-brown and smooth, with lenticels, and finally scaly.

label: Leaves
text: Sixteen to twenty-four inches long, with 11 to 31 toothed, lance-shaped leaflets. Fall color is outstanding.

label: Flowers
text: Dense upright clusters four to eight inches long of tiny greenish-white to yellow flowers in late spring and early summer, male and female on separate plants.

label: Fruit
text: Upright, cone-shaped clusters of hairy drupes on female plants, bright red when ripe and darkening through the winter.

label: Bark
text: Nearly black on mature trunks, shallowly to moderately furrowed into irregular rectangular plates.

label: Leaves
text: Three to nine inches long, with five to seven pointed, bristle-tipped lobes. Leaves in sun are cut more deeply than those in shade. Glossy above, duller and paler beneath.

label: Catkins
text: Yellowish male catkins four to six inches long hang with the new, reddish leaves in May; the female flowers are short spikes of one to four.

label: Acorns
text: Rounded, half to three-quarters of an inch, half covered by a cap of loose scales that form a short fringe at the rim. Trees bear from about twenty, with good crops every two or three years.

label: Bark
text: Scaly on young trees; on mature ones gray to brownish gray, rough, in ridges broken by horizontal cracks into blocks.

label: Leaves
text: Leathery, three to eight inches long, with up to four rounded lobes a side; the upper pair is often much bigger than the rest, giving the leaf the outline of a cross.

label: Catkins
text: Drooping yellowish male catkins in April; the shorter female flowers sit near the twig tips.

label: Acorns
text: Egg-shaped, brown, half to three-quarters of an inch long, alone or in pairs on little or no stalk, a third covered by a cap of small, flat, pale scales.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and reddish brown when young, aging to gray or dark gray-brown with shallow ridges and furrows.

label: Leaves
text: Four to five inches long and about an inch wide, smooth-edged like a willow's, but tipped with a small bristle as red oaks are. Shiny light green above, paler beneath.

label: Catkins
text: Long, hanging yellowish-green male catkins in spring; the female flowers are short spikes.

label: Acorns
text: Rounded, about half an inch long, alone or in pairs, in a shallow, scaly, bowl-shaped cap banded brown and black.

label: Bark
text: Gray to black, with corky ridges and furrows that deepen with age.

label: Leaves
text: Four to seven and a half inches long, narrow and glossy, with straight parallel veins each ending in a bristle-tipped tooth. Golden brown to copper in fall, and often held into winter.

label: Catkins
text: Golden male catkins hang with the new leaves in May; the female flowers are on small spikes.

label: Acorns
text: About an inch long and oval, two-thirds sunk in a cup of long, spreading, curled-back scales like a bird's nest.

label: Bark
