text: Three to five inches, broadly heart-shaped, smooth-edged, leathery and lustrous dark green, with five veins fanning from the base.

label: Needles
text: Glossy, flat needles half an inch to an inch long, on short stalks, lying in two rows either side of the twig. Leaves, seeds and bark are all poisonous.

label: Pollen cones
text: Male plants carry small pollen cones beneath the shoots and shed pollen on warm days in late winter, sometimes so much that the air looks smoky.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online (Taxus baccata, its English parent)

label: Fruit
text: A fleshy red cup around a hard brown seed, borne in fall on female plants only. It is a modified cone, not a berry, and the seed is poisonous.

label: Stems
text: Many stems rise from the base, clothed like its English parent's in thin, red-brown bark that peels.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online (Taxus baccata, its English parent)

label: Bark
text: Ridged and fissured, peeling in thin, fibrous strips.

label: Foliage
text: Two kinds, often on one plant: flat, dark green scale leaves on mature shoots, and sharp, bluish-green needles on young ones.

label: Cones
text: Fleshy, berry-like, blue cones on female plants; the male pollen cones are brown and fall apart when spent.

label: Foliage
text: Mature leaves are tiny scales pressed to the stem in four rows; young ones are awl-like, in pairs. New growth is yellow-green.

label: Cones
text: Blue, berry-like cones under half an inch, with two or three seeds, on short curved stalks. They ripen in their second year.

label: Winter color
text: A low, spreading mat whose green to blue-green summer foliage often takes on a purplish tinge in winter.

label: Needles
text: Stiff, under an inch and a half, in tufts of ten to thirty on short spur shoots, curving toward the tip. Color varies from bright green to silvery blue.

label: Bark
text: Dark gray and fissured, breaking into small scaly plates, and fragrant.

label: Needles
text: Three-quarters of an inch to an inch and a half, stiff, dark green to almost black-green with silvery blue lines, thirty to forty in a tuft on each spur shoot.

label: Cones
text: Upright, barrel-shaped, three to five inches long, purple-brown, with a flat or slightly sunken top. They break apart on the branch, shedding seed from ripening until spring.

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown, ridged and furrowed.

label: Leaves
text: Three to eight inches long, glossy, oval with a long point and a toothed edge, like an elm's; mature leaves look slightly wrinkled. The twigs have no bud at their tips.

label: Bark
text: Dark red-brown to silvery brown, fibrous, in many thin vertical ridges.

label: Foliage
text: Tiny, rounded, overlapping leaves up to a third of an inch, with a blue-gray bloom, on slender shoots that stand straight up from the branches.

label: Fall color
text: A deciduous conifer: in fall the upright shoots turn bright orange to rusty brown.

label: Shape
text: An open, pyramidal tree, slow to grow: about 35 feet after twenty years, though old trees reach 70. A large taproot anchors it, even in standing water.

label: Leaves
text: Glossy and broad, four to eight inches across, usually with three pointed, coarsely toothed lobes and a heart-shaped base. Young shoots carry smaller leaves of three separate leaflets, tinged bronze.

label: Berries
text: Dull, dark bluish-black berries up to a third of an inch, hidden under the leaves until they drop in fall.

label: Fall color
text: Green turning to burgundy and red in a spectacular show; once they fall, the berries they hid come into view.

label: Catkins
text: Silvery-green to yellow catkins in April and May, on separate male and female trees; the male ones, one to two inches long, are the showier.

label: Leaves
text: Three to six inches long and only half to three-quarters of an inch wide, finely toothed and long-pointed, light green above and grayish beneath. The twigs are reddish to yellowish brown and smooth.

label: Flowers
text: Six to twelve fragrant, pale yellow to cream flowers hang in each cluster from a long, strap-like bract.

label: Leaves
text: Small for a linden, two to three inches long and wide, with three to five pointed, toothed lobes, almost like a maple's. Dark green above, paler beneath; a mild yellow in fall.

label: Needles
text: Half an inch to an inch long, widest near the blunt tip, dark green with two whitish bands beneath; the upper ones point forward and up.

label: Cones
text: Upright cones an inch and a half to two and a half inches long. The bracts are much longer than the scales and bent sharply back, which tells Fraser fir from balsam fir.

label: Bark
text: Flaky from a young age, gray to silvery gray; on old trees gray-brown, scaly and rough.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Needles
text: Half to three-quarters of an inch long and four-sided, crowding forward and upward along the shoot. Each lasts three or four years.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Cones
text: The smallest cones of any spruce, with thin scales rounded and smooth at the edge. They ripen in August or September.
source: Morton Arboretum; Silvics of North America

label: Pollen cones
text: Dense pollen cones about half an inch long. The seed cones ripen two or three months after the pollen is shed.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Silvics of North America

label: Flowers
text: Pink buds open to fragrant white flowers about an inch across, covering the shrub in spring, often heavily only every other year.

label: Fruit
text: Half-inch crabapples, yellow to red, ripening in fall and lasting long on the branches.

label: Leaves
text: Dark green, some with side lobes, turning yellow in fall against the red fruit. The young branches are purple and finely hairy.

label: Bark
text: Shiny gray-brown and scaly, but thin: a knock from a mower or trimmer wounds it easily.
source: University of Connecticut Plant Database; University of Florida

label: Bark
text: Reddish brown on young stems, turning pale and shaggy, the outer bark peeling in long, tan strips over a darker layer.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Fruit
text: Small round purplish-red fruits about a third of an inch, each held in sepals that turn from green to purplish red after the petals fall, so the shrub seems to bloom twice.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum

label: Leaves
text: Three to six inches long, in pairs, with smooth, slightly wavy edges.

label: Flowers
text: The buds appear in early summer but wait until late summer to open: small, fragrant, white, in whorls within branched clusters about six inches long.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Morton Arboretum

label: Bark
text: Reddish brown, thick, spongy and fibrous, deeply furrowed.

label: Foliage
text: Bluish-green leaves an eighth to half an inch long, awl-shaped and three-sided, pointing forward along the twig. Older twigs shed them and turn reddish brown and scaly.

label: Cones
text: Oval and woody, about two inches long, green to reddish brown. They reach full size by August of their first year.

label: Pollen cones
text: Tiny round pollen cones, a fifth of an inch or so, one at the tip of each shoot, on the same branches as the seed cones.

label: Leaves
text: An inch and a half to three and a half inches long, in pairs, with three forward-pointing triangular lobes, smooth-edged; glossy green above, whitish beneath. Yellow, orange and red in fall.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Fruit
text: Paired samaras about an inch long, the wings set at varying angles, ripening from August into fall.

label: Bark
text: Gray-brown to orange-brown and slightly corky on young trees, breaking into fissures and scales; old trunks become fluted.
source: Oregon State University Landscape Plants; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Four to six inches across with five lobes, each lobe notched and ending in a rounded point; olive green beneath, with tufts of hair in the vein angles. A cut leafstalk bleeds milky sap.

label: Leaves
text: Four to six inches across, thin, cut half to two-thirds of the way in into nine to eleven double-toothed lobes; densely white-downy beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Small flowers in clusters at the shoot tips, the sepals reddish purple, the petals white to cream.

label: Fall color
text: In its native forests it turns yellow, orange and red, a brilliant sight; some garden trees disappoint, keeping dull brown leaves on the twigs a while before they fall.

label: Bark
text: Silvery gray and smooth on young trees, as both parents' bark is; the plates come later.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Leaves
text: Usually five-lobed, closer to a silver maple's, but the middle lobe is seldom cut into lobes of its own as a silver maple's usually is. Fall color runs from red to yellow.

label: Fruit
text: Paired samaras an inch and a quarter to two and a half inches long, the wings finely lined. Some named forms, such as 'Marmo', are male trees and set no seed at all.

label: Bark
text: Reddish brown on young trees, then chalky gray-white, close and never peeling. Trunks often grow in clumps, a little twisted.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Leaves
text: Two to three inches long, triangular and drawn out into a long tip, shallowly double-toothed, glossy dark green; they hang and flutter on slender stalks.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Catkins
text: The male catkin waits through winter, thin and usually alone at the very tip of the twig; the female catkins are much smaller.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Morton Arboretum

label: Seed catkins
text: Firm cylinders up to an inch long on stout stalks, upright to drooping; the central lobe of each scale points forward.

label: Leaves
text: Half an inch to two and a quarter inches long, widest toward the tip, with three or five shallow rounded or pointed lobes, toothed, dark glossy green.

label: Flowers
text: White, five-eighths of an inch across, six to twelve together in May, with red anthers and two or three styles in each flower.

label: Fruit
text: Red, roundish haws a quarter to three-quarters of an inch long, each with two or three stones. Thorns about an inch long arm the twigs.

label: Bark
text: Shreddy or scaly on young stems. Older trunks are weakly furrowed and often fluted or knotted, until the trunk looks like a twisted bundle of thin stems.

label: Leaves
text: Ten to twelve inches long, compound, of toothed leaflets. Buff-yellow in late summer, deep yellow in fall. In winter, look for the black buds.

label: Flowers
text: Short, dense clusters of tiny flowers from the joints of last year's twigs in April, before the leaves.

label: Trunk
text: The trunk of one of Europe's largest broadleaf trees, up to 140 feet in the best sites. The bark is pale and fissured; the young twigs are smooth and gray.

label: Keys
text: Winged seeds about an inch and a half long, hanging in large bunches; trees bear them in great numbers. The tip of the wing may be blunt, notched or pointed.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Flowers
text: Large, upright goblets of nine tepals on the bare branches in spring, white inside and stained pink to purple at the base outside; color and size vary between the many cultivars.

label: Leaves
text: Up to eight inches long, broadly oval to widest above the middle, glossy dark green above and paler beneath, with fine hairs along the midrib and main veins.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and gray, often marked by sapsuckers with neat horizontal rows of small holes. Large, hairy flower buds sit at the twig tips a year ahead of bloom.

label: Fruit
text: Knobbly, cone-like clusters about two inches long; red-orange seeds slip out of slits.

label: Leaves
text: Thick, leathery and glossy dark green, broadly triangular, with three or five lobes on the climbing and creeping shoots.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Flowers
text: Round heads of small yellowish-green flowers in October, only on the bushy, rootless branches it makes once it reaches the top of its support.

label: Berries
text: Black, berry-like fruits that form late in autumn and ripen in late winter, an important food for birds at that time of year; the birds also carry ivy into the woods.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Climbing stems
text: Climbing stems grip bark with short aerial rootlets. Along the ground the same stems root wherever they touch soil and send up new shoots.
source: Morton Arboretum; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Trunk
text: Usually one straight trunk under a narrow, round-topped crown, its branches upright at first and spreading level with age. It may also grow as a thicket.
source: Fire Effects Information System (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Leaves
text: An inch and a half to four inches long and narrow, finely toothed.
source: Fire Effects Information System (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Flowers
text: White, about half an inch across, on long stalks, five to seven together in small clusters, opening with the leaves.
source: Silvics of North America (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Fruit
text: Small, light red cherries a quarter inch across, each with one large stone, ripening in July.
source: Silvics of North America (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Needles
text: Stiff, sharp needles in whorls of three. Unlike most junipers, it never makes scale leaves: the foliage stays needle-like all its life.
source: Fire Effects Information System (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Cones
text: Berry-like cones, green at first, ripening to a waxy bluish black. Fertilization takes until their second year.
source: Fire Effects Information System (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Bark
text: Thin and smooth, conspicuously speckled with pale lenticels.
source: Fire Effects Information System (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Leaves
text: Broad, oblong to oval, with toothed edges.
source: Fire Effects Information System (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Catkins
text: Male catkins in clusters of two to four, hanging an inch to three inches long; the small female catkins sit nearby.
source: Fire Effects Information System (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Cones
text: Small, woody, cone-like catkins under an inch long, two to six together, holding narrowly winged nutlets.
source: Fire Effects Information System (U.S. Forest Service)

label: Canes
text: Upright canes that live two years, round and smooth but set with slender, straight prickles, and covered in a waxy bloom that shows best in winter.

label: Leaves
text: Four to nine inches long, finely cut into seven to thirteen coarsely toothed leaflets that shrink toward the tip; dark glossy green with silky hairs above and white-felted beneath, the stalk prickly.

label: Bark
text: Pale gray to gray, fissured lengthwise.

label: Leaves
text: An inch and a half to four inches, broadest above the middle with a long tip, doubly toothed, with twelve to twenty-two pairs of veins; downy when young, later smooth but for tufts of hair where the veins meet beneath.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches long, usually three-lobed and coarsely toothed, medium to dark green and sometimes shiny. A modest yellow in fall.

label: Seed capsules
text: Brown, five-part capsules about three-quarters of an inch long that split open and hang on through the winter.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches long, usually three-lobed and coarsely toothed, medium to dark green and sometimes shiny. A modest yellow in fall.

label: Flowers
text: White, two to four inches across, with crepe-like petals around a frilled center; each flower lasts a single day, but new ones open all summer.

label: Seed capsules
text: Brown, five-part capsules about three-quarters of an inch long that split open and hang on through the winter.

label: Flowers
text: Fans of flowering branches open at the tops of the stalks above narrow leaves; this selection keeps flowering through August.

label: Flowers
text: Fans of flowering branches on tall stalks above a fountain of slender, narrow, arching leaves. This selection sets little seed.

label: Canes
text: Upright, bristly canes.

label: Leaves
text: Divided into three to five toothed leaflets, wrinkled along the veins, paler and fuzzy beneath.

label: Flowers
text: Small white flowers in clusters, each with five petals and a cone-shaped center that becomes the fruit, April to June.

label: Flowers
text: Clusters four to six inches long, often in pairs, of pale lavender to lilac-purple flowers, very fragrant.

label: Stems
text: Several stems from the base, the bark thin and smooth, ridged on older wood.

label: Leaves
text: Dark green, in opposite pairs, deeply veined, the surface pleated between the veins.

label: Flowers
text: Flat lacecaps: a center of small fertile flowers ringed by large, showy white sterile ones.

label: Fruit
text: Small, egg-shaped, fleshy fruits in clusters.

label: Fronds
text: Broad, triangular, twice-divided fronds that open bright copper-pink, orange-red and chartreuse, turn glossy dark green by summer and take on coppery tones in fall. They stay up through winter.

label: Leaves
text: Three to five inches long, in opposite pairs, toothed on the upper half, medium to dark green. They hold late into fall.

label: Flowers
text: Bright yellow, inch-long, deeply four-lobed bells, one to six together along last year's bare stems in early spring. Scentless.

label: Foliage
text: Small, glossy scale leaves in flat, dark green sprays that keep their color through winter, on a dense, columnar-pyramidal tree that branches low.

label: Bark
text: Contorted, corkscrew stems under an oval, rounded crown; the twist shows best once the leaves have dropped.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches long and only slightly curled, less twisted than the stems. It is a female clone.

label: Flowers
text: Pale yellow to cream, up to about three inches across, fragrant, opening in spring just before or with the new leaves.

label: Flowers
text: Small yellowish-white flowers in loose sprays three to six inches long, with a scent closer to privet's than to a lilac's.

label: Leaves
text: Two to four inches, oval to lance-shaped and pointed, in opposite pairs; dark green above and grayish green beneath. Little fall color.

label: Seed capsules
text: Oblong, pointed capsules half an inch to an inch long.

label: Leaves
text: Tiny, up to half an inch, oval, dark green with wavy edges, close along stiff branches. Reddish purple in fall.

label: Fruit
text: Round, dark red fruits about a quarter inch across, ripening from late summer into fall, after small white flowers tinged pink in late spring.

label: Trunk
text: Thin and grayish brown, split into thin plates by shallow fissures. Stubs of dead lower branches often linger on the trunk.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Fire Effects Information System

label: Leaves
text: Three to five inches long with five to seven lobes, cut more than halfway to the midrib, ending in bristles; smooth except small tufts of hair in the vein angles beneath.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; University of Minnesota

label: Catkins and new leaves
text: The catkins hang in May as the new leaves open, bright red and hairy at first, green only later.
source: University of Minnesota; Trees and Shrubs Online

label: Acorns
text: Ellipsoid, half to three-quarters of an inch long, a third to half enclosed in a deep, top-shaped cup. The acorn's shape gives the tree its name and best tells it from pin oak.

label: Bark
text: Shiny reddish brown, banded with prominent lenticels.

label: Leaves
text: An inch and a half to three inches long and less than half as wide, oval with a tapering point, sharply and often doubly toothed, downy on the veins beneath, on a short hairy stalk.

label: Flowers
text: Soft rose-pink flowers about three-quarters of an inch across, paling with age, two to five together on short-stalked clusters, each petal notched at the tip.

label: Bark
text: Smooth and silver-gray. The young twigs are covered in white hairs at first but soon turn smooth.

label: Flowers
text: White, from pink buds, in early spring, larger than either parent's.

label: Leaves
text: Two to nearly five inches long, narrowly oval and drawn out to a point, on a short stalk. Smooth, but the edges are fringed with fine hairs.

label: Flowers
text: Half an inch to three-quarters long, in threes or fives at the shoot tips and singly where leaves join the stem. They open pale yellow and darken as they age, so one cluster holds several shades.

label: Seed capsules
text: A dry, woody capsule, long-pointed and vase-shaped, that splits to let its seeds go in September.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Fire Effects Information System

label: Flowers
text: Single flowers an inch to an inch and a half across, opening as the leaves come out. Its name, floribunda, means flowering profusely.

label: Fruit
text: Crabapples three-eighths to half an inch long, yellow flushed with red, colored by late summer and holding on the branches long after.
source: Morton Arboretum; Oregon State University Landscape Plants

label: Leaves
text: One to two and a quarter inches long, leathery and roughly triangular, with two to four toothed lobes on each side. Grayish green beneath, with soft hairs along the veins.

label: Haws
text: About half an inch long, dark red to blackish purple, crowned by the old sepals bent back. Inside, yellowish flesh around one or two seeds, where the common hawthorn has one.
source: Trees and Shrubs Online; Oregon State University Landscape Plants
